name: Red teaming
summary: azure-ai-evaluation RedTeam: attacker/scorer are Microsoft-managed; only the TARGET model accepts BYOM.
description: The Azure AI Evaluation `RedTeam` target can name the model under test as `{connection}/{deployment}`. This routes adversarial probe generation against a BYOM-backed target so users can red-team a gateway-hosted model deployment.
notes:
Red-teaming a BYOM target works, but only if you bypass two `azure-ai-evaluation` SDK bugs by passing a plain-callable target to `rt.scan(target=...)` instead of an `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`. See `test.py`.

> Live scan on 2026-07-16 against `ai-foundry-3swd46vd3j22a`: `overall_total: 2, overall_successful_attacks: 0` — the callable target routes attack prompts through `client.responses.create(model='{apim-conn}/gpt-4o-mini', input=...)` and 2/2 prompts reach the BYOM model as expected.

SDK bugs to fix upstream:

1. **Wrong Entra scope.** `_utils/strategy_utils.py` hardcodes `AZURE_OPENAI_SCOPE = 'https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default'`, but the Foundry BYOM data plane requires `https://ai.azure.com/.default`. Using the wrong scope returns `401 - {'statusCode': 401, 'message': 'Unauthorized. Access token is missing, invalid, audience is incorrect (https://ai.azure.com), or have expired.'}`.
2. **Wrong endpoint.** PyRit's `OpenAIChatTarget` (which the SDK auto-selects when you pass `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`) calls `chat/completions`, but BYOM prefix routing is only exposed on `/openai/v1/responses`. Even with the correct scope, `chat/completions` returns `404 - DeploymentNotFound` because it treats `{conn}/{deployment}` as a literal deployment name. The callable-target workaround uses `responses.create()` directly.
